- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.10) — especially after recent spikes — and adjust downward if sentiment turns neutral or negative.
- Underestimate prices during prolonged negative sentiment (sentiment < -0.15) — model tends to ignore downside risk; increase forecast slightly to account for mean reversion.
- Lagged forecasts often overshoot early in the 30-day horizon — especially when sentiment is volatile — reduce initial forecast by 1–2% to avoid overreaction.
- When sentiment shows strong upward momentum (e.g., 0.27–0.66), model tends to overreact — cap forecast growth at 3–5% above recent 7-day average to avoid inflationary bias.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 3+ days, model underperforms — add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to compensate for suppressed volatility.
- Avoid forecasting sharp upward moves after 2+ consecutive days of high sentiment — model often overcorrects; use smoothing filter or reduce slope of forecast curve.
